doc.title: Jane Monheit interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 20, 2010

title: Why she loves Ella Fitzgerald
summary: Ella's sincerity and musicianship, and her kindness as reported by musicians and her son; a mic adjustment.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Was there something specific you really liked about Ella Fitzgerald?

Everything. Everything. I mean she was a great musician and a brilliant improviser, and sang with such sincerity. I mean you believed Ella. She sang completely — I mean there was no artifice. I mean there was this natural, beautiful thing that came out of her and was absolutely truthful at all times. But then, getting older and knowing musicians that played with her and learning about who she was as a person, I like her even more. The musicians loved her. She was a great musician. She knew exactly what she was doing, and everyone has told me that she was the sweetest, sweetest, loveliest person imaginable. And I’ve met her son, I recorded a song with Ray Brown Junior, and he is the sweetest person imaginable, and I’m just like because your Momma was Ella and I’ve heard that she was so nice. And it makes me love her even more, knowing that not only that she just knew as much as the guys around her did, but that she had this huge loving heart. But how could she not, the way that she sang.
I’m going to ask you to move your mic off your sweater a little bit.
Yeah. We can cut that out.
